A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R3 retrieval framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–K support reliable comparison; the reordered appendices and changed pagination do not represent missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original R3 experiments on five benchmarks, training ablations, transfer analyses and appendix case studies.

after.justification: V2 retains the original R3 benchmark results, ablations, transfer analyses and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain SIDR-based retrieval, offline probability thresholds, online positive/negative sampling and the same combined contrastive loss. The stronger reinforcement-learning framing does not change the documented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, PubHealth and ARC-Challenge, with the same training corpora, datastores and appendix task coverage. Future applications discussed in the prose are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1 and 4 and the ablations is unchanged, including E5, Contriever, DPR/SIDR variants, adaptive retrieval methods, REPLUG, SELF-RAG and RA-DIT. Removed RL citations were not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same accuracy measures, context sizes, model configurations and 80-epoch training protocol. Appendix F still uses 1,000 training instances and top-100 retrieval; other appendix evaluation procedures also match.

E4.justification: Section 5 and appendices retain the offline/online, contrastive-versus-KL and re-indexing ablations, sampling comparisons, probability validation, transfer analysis and IR/RAG case studies. The preliminary study moves from Appendix C to D without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report results without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports R3 one-document accuracy of 47.8 on NQ and 69.5 on PubHealth in both versions; appendix result tables and plotted curves in Figures 4, 5 and 7 also match.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 renames the binary score S as Reward and introduces RAG_theta as shorthand for the existing retrieval-generation composition. The optimization objective, thresholds, losses and probability-generation assumption remain equivalent; the removed RL analogy is conceptual discussion rather than a formal theoretical result.

C1.justification: V2 adds the explicit priority claim that R3 'pioneers reinforcement learning optimization for embedding-based retrievers' in contribution 2 and foregrounds minimal manual tuning in the abstract. V1 lacks that priority claim, while the headline performance, efficiency and conclusion claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 removes the state/action analogy and explicit qualification that the formulation differs from mainstream RL, replacing them with an emphasis on manageable interaction costs and automated retrieval learning. The limitations also refine the proposed use of stronger LLM encoders to specify semi-parametric tuning.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same hyperparameters, hardware/runtime statements, model and datastore descriptions, and prompt templates. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: V2 removes the DPO and PPO references, numbered 54 and 55 in v1, alongside the RL-comparison paragraph; the remaining cited works match after renumbering. The new 'pioneers' claim strengthens novelty positioning without a broader revision of related work.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'via Reinforced Contrastive Learning' to 'via Reinforcement Learning'; the abstract, contributions and portions of Sections 3.1–3.2 are rewritten. Appendices C and D exchange order, with limited heading and prose edits elsewhere; most of the document remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an explicit comparison of CL/RCL signal sources, relevance and training paradigms. Figures 3 and 6 gain explanatory annotations, and existing appendix tables and case-study figures are repositioned. No experimental display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves readability through the revised diagrams, clearer index-staleness explanation and closer placement of case-study figures. However, it strengthens the RL novelty claim while removing v1's explicit qualification about its relationship to mainstream RL, without additional support for that stronger positioning. With the method and empirical evidence unchanged, these presentational benefits and reduced qualification leave the net quality effect uncertain.
